ĭmāgĭno , no
I.perf., ātum, 1, v. a. imago, to give an image of, to represent, fashion (post-class. and very rare): “ut speculum in loco certo positum nihil imaginat, aliorsum translatum facit imagines,” Gell. 16, 18, 3 : “terram digitis suis imaginatam metuere et adorare,” Lact. 5, 13 fin.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
